html:
Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter, born in 1863, best known for The Scream, a figure crying out under a blood-red sky above the Oslo fjord.

Illness and death marked his childhood: his mother and a sister died of tuberculosis. He painted love, fear, jealousy and death with strong colour and twisting lines, in a series he called the Frieze of Life. The Scream exists in several versions from 1893 onwards.

His work in Berlin and Paris helped start Expressionism. The Nazis called it degenerate and removed it from German museums. He left most of his work to the city of Oslo, where the Munch Museum moved to a large new building in 2021. With Ibsen he gave Norway a place in modern European culture.
sum: Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter, born in 1863, best known for The Scream, a figure crying out under a blood-red sky above the Oslo fjord.
